title: Canonical GraphRevisionContent contract, codec and content-hash producer
description:
NEW HEAD OF THE GRAPH BETA CHAIN. Filed 2026-08-17 by architect-2cc07e26 after the human resolved decision dec-64b2391cb80f4c0cbb6e88353017cc65 in favour of OPTION A (full GraphRevisionContent authority). Option B, the non-authoritative structural projection, was REJECTED because it cannot drive Foundation execution and would leave the canary's GAP A open while appearing to progress.

THE AUTHORITY, from the pinned design line 197, verbatim:
  `GraphRevisionContent`: immutable canonical node/edge set, repository base tree,
  parent revision, completion node, policy revision, decomposition budget,
  graph hash, and author.

MEASURED STATE at committed HEAD a42ae2f (git grep against HEAD, not the working tree):
- `git grep -n "GraphRevisionContent" HEAD -- packages/ apps/ | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns ZERO. The type does not exist in code at all.
- @moe/core owns the field that consumes it: `GraphRevisionState.graphContentHash` (packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts:125), validated as hex64 by `validHex64(command.graphContentHash)` (graph-revision-reducer.ts:85) and compared against approval/activation witnesses at :131 and :162. Core treats it as an OPAQUE hex64 string and never computes it.
- @moe/scheduler HAS landed a canonical codec -- packages/scheduler/src/graph-content.ts and graph-content-format.ts, both committed with .js bridges and exported from the root (index.ts:86, :93) -- BUT its own header states "its `graphIdentity` is the only thing hashed", and `graphIdentity` is structural (nodes and edges) only.

THE DEFECT THIS CREATES. The scheduler currently exports a symbol named `graphContentHash` that computes a STRUCTURAL identity covering one of the seven fields design 197 names. Under decision A that name is load-bearing and wrong: a downstream consumer binding a durable revision to it, or any check that greps for the name, passes while carrying an identity that omits the repository base tree, parent revision, completion node, policy revision, decomposition budget and author. This is precisely the "never equate the two hashes" failure the decision was raised to prevent, and it currently sits in a public package root.

Objective: land the canonical GraphRevisionContent contract, its strict codec, and the domain-separated content-hash producer, so a durable graph revision can prove the stored content is the one its approved hash names.

Deliverable: a focused @moe/core production module (core already owns graphContentHash's consumer, so the producer belongs beside it) plus its one-line .js bridge, root export, and focused tests. It COMPOSES the scheduler's canonical snapshot bytes as ONE field -- do not reimplement structural canonicalisation, and do not re-validate the graph; `validateGraphSnapshot` remains the single structural authority.

RELATED RE-SCOPE, not owned by this task but must be coordinated: task-77e8cb4439b148f386d2bbf244c79c16 is BLOCKED with 4 of 6 steps landed. Its work is sound and must be PRESERVED, but its exported name must stop claiming content authority -- rename to a structural name (snapshotIdentity / graphStructureHash) keeping the domain separation. Its retraction message is msg-75057af0. Whoever plans this task should confirm on disk whether that rename has happened, because if it has not, two symbols named for content authority will coexist.

NOT in scope: persistence of the content (that is task-dd4ffa0c), graph lifecycle, daemon transport or ingress, Foundation attempt dispatch, new runtime command or query kinds, or edits to the authoritative design.
definitionOfDone: A public @moe/core GraphRevisionContent contract declares all seven design-197 fields (canonical node/edge set, repository base tree, parent revision, completion node, policy revision, decomposition budget, author) with a bounded shape per field; a test asserts the field set exactly, so a later addition or omission cannot pass silently.

A public producer returns a domain-separated lowercase SHA-256 graphContentHash over ALL seven fields; a test proves changing EACH field individually changes the hash -- assert one case per field and assert the case count equals the field count, so a field silently excluded from the hash is caught.

The producer composes the scheduler's canonical snapshot bytes for the node/edge field and does not reimplement structural canonicalisation or re-validate the graph; a test proves two structurally equivalent node/edge orderings yield the same content hash when all other fields are equal.

The content hash is NEVER equal to the scheduler's structural identity for the same graph: a test asserts the two values differ for a snapshot with non-empty other fields, and asserts the domain separation tag is present, pinning decision dec-64b2391c.

A strict decoder rejects malformed, non-canonical, oversized, extra-keyed, hostile-descriptor/proxy and digest-mismatched bytes under stable core code/layer pairs and never returns content authority; every refusal asserts the exact code and layer and the generated hostile-case count is asserted nonzero.

A mutation drill on the production hash path (drop one field from the hashed input) makes a NAMED per-field test go red for its hash-difference assertion, not for a crash, and production bytes are restored exactly.

The @moe/core root exports the symbols with LF .js bridge and plain-Node loadability coverage; completion names task-dd4ffa0c40834c59892f957fbf61fb23 as the real consumer, and pnpm typecheck && pnpm test report nonzero Test Files counts with each production file <=250 physical lines.
taskRails: Decision dec-64b2391c is RESOLVED as option A: full content authority. Never equate graphContentHash with the scheduler's structural graphIdentity, and never widen the structural identity to stand in for content.

Compose @moe/scheduler's canonical snapshot bytes through its public root as ONE field; do not introduce a second structural graph validator and do not include policy overrides in content identity except via the design-named policy revision field.
Keep the codec deterministic and identical across Windows, macOS and Linux; never depend on filesystem path normalisation, locale ordering, or object key insertion order.

Fail closed with stable reason codes and layers, assert nonzero generated case counts, use TDD, target <=250 lines per production file and split before 400, and commit only explicit owned paths by pathspec.

implementationPlan.description: READ THIS FIRST: the task description says the producer belongs in @moe/core. THAT IS WRONG and the plan overrides it. Confirm on committed HEAD before writing anything. `git show HEAD:packages/core/package.json` shows @moe/core depends on @moe/contracts ONLY; `git show HEAD:packages/scheduler/package.json` shows @moe/scheduler depends on @moe/context, @moe/contracts AND @moe/core. The dependency runs scheduler -> core. Putting a producer in core that composes the scheduler's canonical snapshot bytes would require core -> scheduler and be CIRCULAR. So this work lands in @moe/scheduler, which already owns the validator, the canonical codec, the withheld format mechanics and the GRAPH_CONTENT issue/layer vocabulary, and which can import core types freely. Record that correction in the step note. Then confirm the rest: `git grep "GraphRevisionContent" HEAD -- packages/ apps/` (minus tests) returns ZERO; @moe/core's `GraphRevisionState.graphContentHash` (packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts:125) is an opaque hex64 gated by `validHex64` (graph-revision-reducer.ts:85) and compared at :131 and :162, so core never computes it and this producer must satisfy that exact hex64 spelling.
implementationPlan.note:
MEASURED at HEAD 15918c7 (task description said a42ae2f; HEAD has moved forward — facts re-measured, all still hold).

Dependency edge runs scheduler -> core. A producer in @moe/core composing scheduler canonical snapshot bytes would need core -> scheduler = CIRCULAR, and this repo has no escape hatch (no tsconfig paths, no project references; deep relative import fails TS6059). WORK LANDS IN @moe/scheduler.

REST OF STEP-1 CONFIRMED:
- `git grep -n "GraphRevisionContent" HEAD -- packages/ apps/ | grep -v '\.test\.'` -> ZERO lines (whole-repo grep also zero). Type does not exist in code at all.

- Witness comparisons at graph-revision-reducer.ts:131 (`approval.graphHash !== state.graphContentHash`) and :162 (`activation.graphHash !== state.graphContentHash`). Core stores and compares, never computes.

"Review-qualified goal closure" — a foreign sweep commit, not task-77e8cb44's own. `git status --porcelain -- packages/scheduler/` shows ONLY `M packages/scheduler/src/index.ts`, and that diff is a foreign comment reflow of the lease-drain release-authority block (task-4731ba34 territory), NOT a graph-content rename. implementationPlan.description: Confirm the defect this task exists to fix, and size the edit. Read packages/scheduler/src/graph-content.ts (208 lines) and graph-content-format.ts (184 lines) at HEAD. Facts to verify: (a) `GraphContent` is `{schemaVersion, graphContentHash, snapshot, bytes}` -- snapshot ONLY, none of the other design-197 fields; (b) its `graphContentHash` field comment says "the spelling @moe/core's revision gate requires", so it was built to be handed straight to core's gate -- under decision dec-64b2391c option A that binding is exactly the defect, because a structure-only identity would satisfy core's hex64 check; (c) graph-content-format.ts:110-111 hashes `identity` -- the ValidatedGraph.graphIdentity -- and nothing else; (d) `SCHEMA_TAG = "MOE-GRAPH-CONTENT/1"` (:28) and `HASH_DOMAIN = "MOE-GRAPH-CONTENT-HASH/1"` (:33) already exist and are deliberately separate, so domain separation is a pattern to EXTEND, not invent. Both files are near the 250-line target, so plan the split now: put the new per-field canonicalisation in a NEW sibling module rather than growing either file past cap. Note the deliberate design you must preserve: the root export comment (index.ts:71-77) says `canonicalGraphJson`/`graphContentHash` are WITHHELD from the public surface because a consumer holding them could mint canonical bytes for a snapshot the kernel never accepted, and `encodeGraphContent` is the only route to a hash. Keep that property.
implementationPlan.note:
DEFECT CONFIRMED, all four facts verified by reading the files at HEAD 15918c7.
(a) graph-content.ts:74-80 `GraphContent = {schemaVersion, graphContentHash, snapshot, bytes}` — snapshot ONLY, zero of the other six design-197 fields.
(b) :76 comment verbatim "Lowercase 64-char SHA-256 hex, the spelling @moe/core's revision gate requires" — built to be handed straight to core's validHex64 gate. Under dec-64b2391c option A that binding IS the defect: a structure-only identity satisfies hex64.
(c) graph-content-format.ts:107-113 `graphContentHash(graph)` hashes `graph.graphIdentity` and NOTHING else.
(d) :28 `SCHEMA_TAG = "MOE-GRAPH-CONTENT/1"`, :33 `HASH_DOMAIN = "MOE-GRAPH-CONTENT-HASH/1"`, deliberately separate — pattern to EXTEND.

NEW MEASUREMENT that decides the completion-node question (step-3 asks for it explicitly): `computeGraphIdentity` at packages/scheduler/src/graph-internal.ts:169-187 ALREADY frames the completion node — line 183 `parts.push("C" + frame(view.completionNodeKey))` — and `canonicalGraphJson` (format.ts:100) already serializes it. So the completion node is ALREADY inside the composed snapshot field. DECISION: it is ALSO restated as its own top-level content field (design 197 names it; DoD 1 requires seven declared fields), and the codec REFUSES their disagreement with a new stable code rather than letting two definitions drift. Consequence stated honestly in the test header: that field's digest contribution is functionally determined by the snapshot field, so its per-field sweep case co-varies by construction and is backed by a dedicated drift-refusal case. Drills target independently-variable fields.

SIZES (`wc -l`): graph-content.ts 208, graph-content-format.ts 184, graph-content.test.ts 643, index.ts 423, graph-model.ts 337, runtime-shape.ts 129, validate-graph.ts 80. Both production files near cap -> new sibling module graph-content-fields.ts as planned.

DESIGN CHOSEN (single codec, extended in place per step 5, plus step 6's rename): schema 2 envelope carries `content` (the seven fields) and `hash`; `GraphContent` gains `content` and a SECOND hash field `snapshotIdentity` (the old structure-only value, renamed off the content name per step 6). Both values sit on one envelope, so DoD 4's "never equal" invariant is directly assertable. `snapshotIdentityHash` gets its own digest domain `MOE-GRAPH-SNAPSHOT-IDENTITY/1` so the two can never collide; content gets `MOE-GRAPH-CONTENT-HASH/2`, wire tag `MOE-GRAPH-CONTENT/2`. `snapshotIdentity` is NOT serialized (derived on decode), so there is one fewer forgeable field.

WITHHELD-MECHANICS PROPERTY PRESERVED (index.ts:71-77): `canonicalGraphJson`, `canonicalSnapshotJson`, `snapshotIdentityHash` and the digest fold all stay unexported from the root; `encodeGraphContent` remains the only route to a hash.

RE-READ OF RAIL 2 given step 1's package override: "compose ... through its public root" is unachievable from INSIDE @moe/scheduler; the binding intent (do not reimplement structural canonicalisation, do not add a second validator) is satisfied by composing the internal `canonicalSnapshotJson` split out of the existing `canonicalGraphJson`.

DESIGN CROSS-CHECK for field bounds: design 405 says the decomposition budget is a COMPOSITE (24 nodes, 64 hard edges, depth 3, width 6, nine per expansion). `git grep decompositionBudget HEAD -- packages/ apps/` returns ZERO, so no existing convention. This content field is modelled as the scalar NODE allowance the revision was authored under, ceiling-bound to the kernel's own ABSOLUTE_MAX_GRAPH_NODES rather than a guessed number (same non-guessed pattern as DECODE_POLICY); the remaining budget dimensions are policy-resolved and belong to the goal aggregate, out of scope here.

implementationPlan.description: RED on the contract shape, in the existing packages/scheduler/src/graph-content.test.ts. Define GraphRevisionContent as the SEVEN design-197 fields and write the failing shape tests first. The fields: canonical node/edge set (the existing validated snapshot), repository base tree, parent revision, completion node, policy revision, decomposition budget, author. NOTE while designing: `completionNodeKey` already lives INSIDE GraphSnapshot (packages/scheduler/src/graph-model.ts), so decide explicitly whether it is carried once via the snapshot or restated as its own field, and write the decision in the test file's header -- restating it in two places invites them to disagree. Tests: (1) a well-formed content value encodes and its field set is EXACTLY the declared set, asserted against a frozen expected key list so a later addition or omission fails rather than passing; (2) `parentRevision` is legitimately absent for an INITIAL revision -- assert an explicit absent marker encodes deterministically and is NOT confused with an empty string; (3) each field's bound is enforced (over-long refs, non-hex digests, a negative or non-integer decomposition budget, an empty author) and each refuses with an exact code and layer from the existing frozen GRAPH_CONTENT_ISSUE_CODES / GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS vocabulary -- extend those frozen lists rather than inventing a parallel one.
implementationPlan.note:
RED CONFIRMED: `npx vitest run --root . packages/scheduler/src/graph-content.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 37 failed | 9 passed (46)`. Nonzero executed count, so the run is real, not a vacuous filter.

COMPLETION-NODE DECISION, written into the test file header (lines 25-49) as step 3 required. Measured basis: `computeGraphIdentity` (graph-internal.ts:169-187) already frames the completion node as `"C" + frame(view.completionNodeKey)`, and `canonicalGraphJson` already serializes it inside the snapshot. DECISION: it is ALSO declared as its own design-197 field, as the AUTHOR'S DECLARATION, and the codec reconciles the two in exactly one place — `GRAPH_CONTENT_COMPLETION_DRIFT` / `GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY` on any disagreement, on BOTH encode and decode. The header states the honest consequence rather than hiding it: because the declaration is pinned equal to the graph's value, its digest contribution is functionally determined by the snapshot field, so its per-field sweep case CO-VARIES by construction (the kernel makes an independent variation unrepresentable) and its real authority is pinned by the drift-refusal cases. Step-7 drills therefore target independently-variable fields.

TESTS WRITTEN (new describe "GraphRevisionContent — the seven design-197 fields"):
1. FIELD SET EXACTLY: `GRAPH_REVISION_CONTENT_KEYS` compared against a HAND-WRITTEN frozen `EXPECTED_CONTENT_KEYS` (a copy of the production array would agree with any future edit, so duplicating the names here is the point), plus length 7, frozen, sorted, no duplicates. Also asserted on the WIRE: the serialized `content` object's key list must equal the production key list, so a field added to the contract but not serialized reddens.
2. ABSENT parentRevision: `null` encodes deterministically (two independent encodes byte-identical, same hash), the bytes carry the explicit `"parentRevision":null` marker, the initial-revision hash DIFFERS from the with-parent hash, and it survives decode as null. NOT-CONFUSED-WITH-EMPTY is proved the strong way: `""` is not a representable ref at all and refuses with the exact pair, so the two forms are unreachable from one another.
3. PER-FIELD BOUNDS: 26 cases across all six caller-stated fields, each asserting exactly `[["GRAPH_CONTENT_FIELD_INVALID","GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC"]]`, with the covered-field set asserted EQUAL to the declared key set minus `snapshot` (so a field that quietly loses its bound reddens). `snapshot` is excluded deliberately: its judgement belongs to `validateGraphSnapshot`, and a separate case asserts `contentOf(7)` refuses at `GRAPH_MALFORMED_SNAPSHOT` / `GRAPH_VALIDATION` — a codec-layer answer there would mean the field reader had taken over structural judgement.
4. HOSTILE CONTENT: 10 cases (count asserted >= 10) — non-object, null, array, proxy, extra key, missing key, symbol key, two accessor-descriptor fields, prototype-bearing record — all at the codec layer.
5. Drift refused on encode AND on decode (bytes hand-edited so the declaration disagrees with the graph).

VOCABULARY DISCIPLINE: two new codes only — `GRAPH_CONTENT_COMPLETION_DRIFT` and `GRAPH_CONTENT_FIELD_INVALID` — added to the EXISTING frozen `GRAPH_CONTENT_ISSUE_CODES` (sorted position verified), no new layers, and the existing "emits every declared codec code from a real path" test extended with a producing path for each so neither code can be a guard the module only claims to have.

NO SECOND REF VOCABULARY INVENTED: `parentRevision`, `policyRevision`, `completionNode` and `author` are all bounded by the existing `isGraphKey` (graph-key.ts) — ASCII-only, <=MAX_GRAPH_KEY_CODE_UNITS, path-unsafe characters excluded. `repositoryBaseTree` is lowercase hex40 or hex64 (git SHA-1 and SHA-256 object formats, neither of which the codec should prefer). `decompositionBudget` is a non-negative safe integer ceiling-bound to ABSOLUTE_MAX_GRAPH_NODES, and `-0` is refused rather than silently canonicalised to `0`.

EXISTING 643-LINE SUITE PRESERVED, NOT REWRITTEN: every landed structural assertion now goes through a new `encodeSnapshot()` wrapper that holds the six non-snapshot fields constant, so any hash difference those tests observe is still attributable to structure alone. The wrapper derives `completionNode` from the fixture's own `completionNodeKey`, because otherwise every fixture that moves the completion node would refuse as drift and prove nothing structural.

implementationPlan.description: RED on the hash, which is the heart of the task. Still in graph-content.test.ts. (1) THE PER-FIELD SWEEP required by DoD 2: for EACH of the seven fields, hold the other six constant, change that one, and assert the graphContentHash changes. Assert the generated case count EQUALS the field count -- a sweep that silently skipped a field is exactly how a field gets omitted from the hash while every test stays green, and a bare count-free loop cannot catch it. (2) ORDER INDEPENDENCE: two structurally equivalent node/edge orderings with all other fields equal produce the SAME hash, inherited from validateGraphSnapshot's canonical ordering rather than re-implemented. (3) THE DECISION GUARD, pinning dec-64b2391c: for a content value whose non-snapshot fields are non-empty, assert `graphContentHash !== ` the scheduler's structural identity for the same snapshot, and assert the hash domain tag is present and distinct from the wire schema tag. This is the test that makes the two-hash confusion impossible to reintroduce. (4) DETERMINISM: the same logical content yields byte-identical canonical bytes across two independent encodes, and object key insertion order does not affect the result.
implementationPlan.note:
RED CONFIRMED. `npx vitest run --root . packages/scheduler/src/graph-content.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests no tests`, cause `Error: Cannot find module './graph-content-fields.js'`. The step-3 run before these additions was `37 failed | 9 passed (46)`; the collection now fails earlier because the new tests import the not-yet-created module, which is the expected TDD state.

(1) PER-FIELD SWEEP, the heart of DoD 2. `FIELD_VARIATIONS` is keyed BY FIELD NAME, and the sweep asserts its coverage two ways that a bare loop cannot: `toHaveLength(GRAPH_REVISION_CONTENT_KEYS.length)` AND `FIELD_VARIATIONS.map(([field]) => field)` deep-equal to the production key list. A sweep that generated zero cases, or that silently skipped a field, reddens on those two lines before any hash is compared. Each case then asserts the hash CHANGED, the bytes changed, and no two variations collide, with `seen.size` asserted equal to fieldCount + 1.
Variation choices are deliberate: `snapshot` varies by adding dev-d plus a HARD edge into dev-c, so the completion node is UNCHANGED and that case varies structure alone; `completionNode` varies to a 2-node graph completing at dev-b, and its comment states inline that the two move together because the kernel binds them, pointing at the drift-refusal cases as where that field's authority actually lives.

(2) ORDER INDEPENDENCE: all 36 orderings (3! nodes x 3! edges, count asserted 36) with the other six fields equal yield the SAME graphContentHash and byte-identical output — inherited from validateGraphSnapshot's canonical ordering, not re-derived.

(3) THE DECISION GUARD for dec-64b2391c, built as a PAIR so it cannot be satisfied by returning one value twice: `snapshotIdentity` must be INVARIANT across a change to any non-structural field while `graphContentHash` must MOVE (asserted over the five non-structural variations, count asserted = fieldCount - 2), and `snapshotIdentity` must MOVE when structure moves. Plus: the two are never equal on either graph; both digest domains and the wire tag are three distinct strings (`MOE-GRAPH-CONTENT-HASH/2`, `MOE-GRAPH-SNAPSHOT-IDENTITY/1`, `MOE-GRAPH-CONTENT/2`), asserted against the production constants; neither digest domain appears in the bytes while the wire tag does (a serialized domain could not be rotated independently); the structural identity is NOT on the wire at all, so no reader is handed a second, weaker value to bind to; and neither hash equals the raw graphIdentity string.

(4) DETERMINISM: two independent encodes are byte-identical with equal hashes, AND a content record whose seven keys are declared in REVERSE order (insertion order asserted reversed against the production key list) produces byte-identical output and the same hash — a codec that serialized or hashed caller key order would give one logical content two identities.

(5) LENGTH FRAMING, added beyond the step's four items because an unframed fold is a forgery surface, not a bug: two contents whose parentRevision+policyRevision concatenations are asserted BYTE-IDENTICAL ("rev-ab"+"polcd" vs "rev-abpol"+"cd") must still hash differently. Without per-field framing they collide.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN. Create the new sibling module packages/scheduler/src/graph-content-fields.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./graph-content-fields.ts";` -- without it the module is invisible to the .js import graph) holding the per-field bounded validation and canonical encoding for the six non-snapshot fields. Then extend graph-content-format.ts to fold ALL seven fields into the digest -- today :110-111 hashes only `identity` -- keeping the existing length-framed, domain-separated construction so no field can be smuggled across a boundary into another. Extend graph-content.ts's `GraphContent` to carry the full content, keeping `graphContentHash` spelled as the lowercase 64-char hex @moe/core's gate requires. BUMP THE SCHEMA: `GRAPH_CONTENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1 -> 2, `SCHEMA_TAG` and `HASH_DOMAIN` to their /2 spellings. The wire shape is changing and the existing frozen issue code `GRAPH_CONTENT_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA` already exists, so version-1 bytes must decode to that clean refusal rather than being silently reinterpreted -- add a test for it. Keep every file at or under 250 physical lines; if format.ts cannot absorb the fold, move the digest construction into the new module rather than trimming a guard.

Publish the surface and separate the two identities by NAME, which is the rename half of this lane's problem. Update packages/scheduler/src/index.ts to export the GraphRevisionContent type and the extended codec. THE STRUCTURAL IDENTITY MUST STOP WEARING THE CONTENT NAME: whatever the root currently publishes that resolves to a structure-only value must be named for what it is (snapshotIdentity / graphStructureHash), so a consumer cannot reach a structural value by asking for content. Preserve the withheld-mechanics property from index.ts:71-77 -- `encodeGraphContent` stays the only route to a hash, and the raw canonicalisation helpers stay unexported. Extend the existing root-export/bridge guard tests so the new symbols are covered, and verify plain-Node loadability of the new `.js` bridge from a consumer package. COORDINATE, do not collide: task-77e8cb44 is BLOCKED with 4 of 6 steps landed and committed and owns overlapping files. Before editing, `git log -1 -- packages/scheduler/src/graph-content*.ts` and re-read those files; if its rename has already landed, adopt the name it chose instead of inventing a second one, and say so in the step note.

Mutation drills, three, one per claim a green suite cannot otherwise distinguish. Drill 1 (every field is really hashed) -- the DoD-6 drill: remove ONE field from the hashed input in the digest construction; the step-4 per-field case for that field must go RED on its hash-difference assertion, not on a crash. Repeat for a second, different field so the drill proves the sweep rather than one lucky case. Drill 2 (the two hashes stay separate): make the content hash fall back to the structural identity; the step-4 decision guard must go RED. This is the drill that protects dec-64b2391c. Drill 3 (the schema bump is load-bearing): make the decoder accept version-1 bytes; the unsupported-schema test must go RED. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME and the exact assertion -- a drill that reddens by crashing, or on a different assertion, has not proven the binding. Restore exact bytes by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in this shared worktree), and confirm with `git diff --numstat` showing 0 added and 0 deleted per drilled file. One drill at a time: a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch and leave git reading clean.

Adversarial review, then commit and gate. ATTACKER PASS: can any consumer obtain a graphContentHash without going through the encoder, reopening the withheld-mechanics seam? Can two different logical contents collide -- are all seven fields length-framed so a value cannot bleed across a boundary? Can a hostile descriptor, getter or revoked proxy on the input object be read twice with different answers (snapshot hostile input before inspecting it)? Is the encoding stable across Windows, macOS and Linux, free of filesystem path normalisation and locale-sensitive ordering? Does an absent parentRevision encode distinctly from an empty string? Does any refusal reuse a code that means something else? Confirm every production file is <=250 physical lines and that no second structural validator was introduced. Name `task-dd4ffa0c40834c59892f957fbf61fb23` as the real consumer in the completion note, and state that task-77e8cb44, task-32c1ba45, task-eacea969, task-931f99e8 and task-c4b80778 are all blocked on this surface. COMMIT: `git status --porcelain`, unstage foreign entries with `git restore --staged -- <path>`, commit ONLY the owned paths by explicit pathspec, verify with `git show --stat`. GATE, foreground and `&&`-chained so no red leg is masked: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test`, plus a plain-Node import of the new bridge. Read the OUTPUT: a filtered leg is evidence only if it prints a `Test Files N passed` line with N nonzero, since `pnpm --filter` on an unresolved name prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: THE PLAN OVERRIDES ITS OWN TASK DESCRIPTION ON ONE POINT. I filed this task saying the producer belongs in @moe/core, because core owns the consuming field. Measuring the manifests refutes it: @moe/core depends on @moe/contracts ONLY, while @moe/scheduler depends on @moe/context, @moe/contracts AND @moe/core. A core-hosted producer composing scheduler snapshot bytes needs core -> scheduler and is circular. So the work lands in @moe/scheduler, which already owns validateGraphSnapshot, the canonical codec, the withheld format mechanics and the GRAPH_CONTENT issue/layer vocabulary, and which imports core freely. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (a) a new package for the contract -- an entire workspace package, manifest, lock importer and bridge set for one contract that has exactly one natural home; (b) adding @moe/scheduler to @moe/core's dependencies -- circular, and there is no escape hatch in this repo (no tsconfig paths, no project references; a deep relative import fails TS6059); (c) building it in apps/daemon -- it would stop being a shared contract and every package needing content identity would deep-import a daemon module; (d) extending the existing GraphContent in place without a schema bump -- the wire shape changes, and silently reinterpreting version-1 bytes under version-2 rules is how a structure-only hash survives as if it were content; the frozen code GRAPH_CONTENT_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA already exists precisely for this. CHOSE: extend the scheduler's existing content surface to all seven design-197 fields, bump schema/tag/domain to /2, add a sibling module for per-field canonicalisation so neither existing file crosses the line cap, and rename the structural identity off the content name.

planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is a field that is declared but never hashed: the contract would look complete, every shape test would pass, and revisions would bind to an identity missing (say) the author or the decomposition budget. Only a per-field sweep whose CASE COUNT is asserted equal to the field count catches it -- a loop without the count assertion passes while silently skipping a field, and drill 1 exists to prove the sweep is real. Second risk is the two-hash confusion this whole decision exists to prevent: the scheduler currently publishes a structure-only value under the content name, so the easiest possible mistake is to keep returning it; the step-4 decision guard and drill 2 pin it, and step 6 renames it so the mistake is not reachable by autocomplete. Third, the schema bump: without it, version-1 bytes decode under version-2 rules and a structure-only hash survives disguised as content. Fourth, length-framing every field -- without it two different contents can collide by shifting bytes across a field boundary, which is a forgery, not a bug. Fifth, hostile input must be snapshotted before inspection; a getter or revoked proxy read twice can answer differently between validation and hashing. Sixth, determinism across Windows/macOS/Linux: no path normalisation, no locale ordering, no reliance on object key insertion order. Seventh, an absent parentRevision (initial revision) must encode distinctly from an empty string. Finally, FILE COLLISION: task-77e8cb44 has landed committed work in exactly these files and is blocked pending a rename -- re-read them and adopt its chosen name if present rather than inventing a competing one, and never reset its work.
